s: Safety and compliance layers that validate, filter, and constrain LLM inputs and outputs to prevent harmful, biased, off-topic, or policy-violating content.
w: Guardrails intercept requests before they reach the LLM and responses before they reach the user. Input guardrails check for prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, PII exposure, and topic restrictions. Output guardrails scan for toxicity, hallucinated facts, policy violations, sensitive data leakage, and format compliance. Rules are defined as configurable policies (block, warn, transform, redact). Guardrails can use lightweight classifiers for speed or full LLM calls for nuanced evaluation. They operate as middleware in the request/response pipeline with sub-100ms latency requirements.
use: Preventing prompt injection and jailbreak attacks on production LLM applications
Redacting PII (names, emails, SSNs) from LLM inputs and outputs
Ensuring LLM responses comply with brand safety and content policies
Filtering harmful, biased, or off-topic content before it reaches users
avoid: Overly restrictive guardrails that block legitimate use cases (false positive rate matters)
Guardrails as the sole safety layer - defense in depth requires multiple controls
Deep inspection guardrails on every request where latency budget is tight

props.action_on_violation: What to do: block, warn, redact, or substitute with safe response
props.policy_set: Which guardrail rules to enforce for this request path

pat.d: Fast classifiers for high-volume pre-filtering, LLM-based checks on borderline cases, human review for ambiguous violations.
Detect PII or sensitive content, redact in input, pass sanitized version to LLM, restore in output if needed.

pits: Over-blocking legitimate content frustrates users - track false positive rates and tune thresholds
Guardrail latency adding to total response time - place fast checks first, slow checks async
Adversarial attacks evolving faster than guardrail rules - continuous red teaming needed
tips: Layer guardrails: fast regex/rule-based checks first, ML classifiers second, LLM judges third
Log all guardrail actions for post-hoc analysis and policy refinement
Treat guardrails as product features, not just engineering concerns - user trust depends on them
